title.narrative: A Regional Pathway to Rights-based Climate and Nature Action

description.narrative:
SPDA’s project “Bosques Resilientes: A Regional Pathway to Rights-based Climate and Biodiversity Action” is a locally led initiative that strengthens forest governance, safeguards Indigenous rights, and combats environmental crime across Peru and Colombia. The project responds to escalating deforestation, weak governance, and the vulnerability of Indigenous and local communities who serve as key forest stewards.
Led by Sociedad Peruana de Derecho Ambiental (SPDA) and ProPurús in Peru, the consortium will deliver activities and outputs contributing to outcomes across the the project countries. Its overall objective is to advance inclusive, rights-based forest and land-use governance that reduces forest loss, strengthens biodiversity conservation, and supports climate mitigation.
Secondary objectives include securing Indigenous territorial rights, promoting sustainable livelihoods and women’s leadership, enhancing community-based forest monitoring, protecting environmental defenders, and institutionalizing regional learning and adaptive management.
The project aligns with ODA eligibility rules by addressing poverty, inequality, and climate vulnerability through capacity building, rights recognition, and sustainable economic opportunities for marginalized groups. It contributes directly to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and national commitments under REDD+ and NDCs. Strategic partnerships include Indigenous people's organisations such as FENAMAD and ORPIO, alongside local governments, civil society, and universities. By embedding Indigenous leadership and cross-border collaboration, the initiative will generate lasting regional impact in the Amazon.
